Paris, May 1934.

From the notebook of Marie Curie, physicist, twice laureate of the Nobel Prize, Director of the Radium Institute.

The weather this week has been fair, and I have been able to resume the measurements postponed since the winter. This morning I reviewed the accounts of the Institute and signed the order for the new electrometer. There is a letter from Debierne still to answer, and the proofs of the memoir on the radioactive constants are late from the printer. Yesterday I said to my assistant:

"We are not going to be able to finish the measurements before the holidays. What should we do with them?" "We must finish," she replied. I am not sure that it is a good idea to be so ambitious.
